finding.claim: The ban endpoint catches the 403 raised by require_admin and carries on, so any authenticated non-admin user can ban any user. abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException, which subclasses Exception. The `except Exception` handler only logs a warning and then falls through to do_ban(uid).
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sends POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid. g.user.is_admin is falsy.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the privileged ban operation.

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST with an attacker-controlled uid.
require_admin(g.user) calls abort(403) for a non-admin (admin.py:9-11), which raises HTTPException.
Handler only logs a warning. It does not re-raise or return.
do_ban(uid) runs unconditionally and the endpoint returns ok=True.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only authorization control on this path and it is neutralised by the swallowed exception. There is no decorator, before_request hook, or other check in the file. The unban route (admin.py:26) calls require_admin without a try/except, so it is correctly protected. A non-admin also gets a warning log containing their name, which does not stop the ban.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the abort is swallowed by `except Exception` at admin.py:18-19. The file has no decorator or before_request hook. The unban route (admin.py:26) calls require_admin without a try/except.
verdict.reason: admin.py:11 abort(403) raises an HTTPException, which `except Exception` at admin.py:18 catches. admin.py:19 only logs, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any non-admin caller who reaches the route. The only difference from the candidate's wording is that it says `g.user.is_admin`, whereas the code uses `user.get("is_admin")`, which has the same effect.
